subject: Numeracy
title: Our maths celebration
objectives: Children will show year learning through games and a maths fair.
Teachers will complete every child’s end-of-year record and transition note.
content: Revising number and counting, shape and measures, and celebrating the year with end-of-year records and a transition note.
teachingActivities: Keep every activity familiar and joyful; observe quietly; record how far each child counts and how well they solve small problems; invite parents to the celebration; complete the transition note honestly for the Nursery 2 teacher.
learnerActivities: Show learning from the year through games and a small maths fair.
assessment: Observe and record each child’s end-of-year numeracy learning and complete the transition note.
expectedOutcomes: Takes part confidently in familiar maths games.
Each child has an end-of-year observation record.

lessons.title: Revising number and counting
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit counting, numerals, more and fewer, joining and taking away through games.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt number, shape, measure, time, data, money, position and number stories this year.
lessons.starter: Sing the counting song and say "Today we play our favourite number games."
teacherActivities: Play the dice and counters game.
Play one more and one less on the number line.
Play join and take away stories.
Let each child choose a favourite game.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play the dice and counters game. Children: Child throws and counts.
Step 2. Teacher: Play one more and one less on the number line. Children: Child steps forward and back.
Step 3. Teacher: Play join and take away stories. Children: Child solves with objects.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a favourite game. Children: Child chooses and plays.

practical.title: Number games
steps: Children play each for five minutes.
practical.safety: Supervise each area and use large counters. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child with numbers up to five.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a game.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Joins and takes away with confidence
lessons.conclusion: Count to twenty and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep playing number games over the holiday.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit counting, numerals, more and fewer, joining and taking away through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Revising shape and measures
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit shapes, patterns, size, weight, capacity and time through games.
successCriteria: Names five shapes and makes a pattern
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt number, shape, measure, time, data, money, position and number stories this year.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we play shape and measuring games."
teacherActivities: Play the feely bag with five shapes.
Use the balance to compare two objects.
Pour water and say full or empty.
learnerActivities: Child feels and names a shape.
Child pours and says full or empty.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play the feely bag with five shapes. Children: Child feels and names a shape.
Step 2. Teacher: Make a bead pattern. Children: Child threads a pattern.
Step 3. Teacher: Use the balance to compare two objects. Children: Child says which is heavier.
Step 4. Teacher: Pour water and say full or empty. Children: Child pours and says full or empty.

practical.title: Shape and measure games
steps: Children play each for four minutes.
practical.safety: Supervise each area and wipe spills at once. Use large smooth shapes and beads and shallow water.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child with two objects.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a pattern and compare weights.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the materials away and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep looking for shapes and measuring at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit shapes, patterns, size, weight, capacity and time through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Maths fair stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s end-of-year numeracy at a small maths fair.
successCriteria: Shows number, shape, measure, time and money knowledge
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt number, shape, measure, time, data, money, position and number stories this year.
lessons.starter: Say "Today is our maths fair. We visit six stations and show what we know."
teacherActivities: Set up six stations: counting, numerals, shapes, measures, money and stories.
Observe each child at two stations and record what they do.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up six stations: counting, numerals, shapes, measures, money and stories. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Observe each child at two stations and record what they do. Children: Children play at stations.
Step 3. Teacher: Take photographs and make notes. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Maths fair
steps: Set up six stations with familiar materials.
practical.safety: Supervise each station with an adult or helper. Keep water shallow, play money large and floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and stay at familiar stations.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show friends how a station works.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: counts to 20 and counts objects; names numerals; names five shapes; compares measures; uses play money; solves number stories.

lessons.conclusion: Say well done to everyone and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a favourite maths game at home during the holiday.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s end-of-year numeracy at a small maths fair" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Maths celebration
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will celebrate the year with number songs and games and show their work to visitors.
successCriteria: Shows something they enjoyed to an adult
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt number, shape, measure, time, data, money, position and number stories this year.
resources: Children’s graphs, shape pictures and patterns
lessons.starter: Say "Today we celebrate everything we counted, measured and made. Let us sing our favourite number songs."
teacherActivities: Sing favourite number rhymes with actions.
Invite children to show their work to a visitor or parent.
Give each child a sticker or certificate and say their name.
learnerActivities: Child waves and says thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing favourite number rhymes with actions. Children: Children sing and do actions.
Step 2. Teacher: Invite children to show their work to a visitor or parent. Children: Child shows their work.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child a sticker or certificate and say their name. Children: Child waves and says thank you.

practical.title: Celebration circle
steps: Sit in a circle with visitors.
practical.safety: Check for allergies before any snack and use non-toxic stickers. Supervise visitors and keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and share their work together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose the last song.

assessment.method: Complete each child’s end-of-year numeracy record from the year’s observations. Note the highest number counted accurately, a strength and a next step for Nursery 2.

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "See you in Nursery 2."
lessons.homeConnection: Keep counting, measuring and noticing shapes over the holiday.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "celebrate the year with number songs and games and show their work to visitors" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Transition note and records
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will complete a transition note for each child for the Nursery 2 teacher.
successCriteria: Records what each child can do
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt number, shape, measure, time, data, money, position and number stories this year.
lessons.starter: Today the children enjoy free play with familiar materials while the teacher completes the transition notes.
teacherActivities: Set out free play with blocks, shapes, a play market and number games.
Review each child’s three term records and portfolio.
Complete the note: strengths, counting range, shapes, measures, problem solving and next steps.
learnerActivities: Children play while the teacher reviews.
Children play and talk with the helper.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set out free play with blocks, shapes, a play market and number games. Children: Children play freely and happily.
Step 2. Teacher: Review each child’s three term records and portfolio. Children: Children play while the teacher reviews.
Step 3. Teacher: Complete the note: strengths, counting range, shapes, measures, problem solving and next steps. Children: Children play and talk with the helper.

practical.title: Free play and records
steps: Set out four play areas with a helper.
The teacher reviews records at a quiet table.
The teacher completes each transition note.
practical.safety: A second adult must supervise play while the teacher completes the notes. Keep all areas safe and tidy.

differentiation.support: Offer familiar toys and a helper nearby.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to help a friend tidy up.

assessment.method: Write for each child: how far they count; numeral recognition; use of more, fewer, one more and one less; joining and taking away; shapes and patterns; measures; interests; any support needed; and a next step. Use the four-level scale and facts you have seen.

questions.question: What do you like to play?
What did you enjoy this year?

expectedOutcomes: Has a transition note for each child
lessons.conclusion: Tidy up together and say goodbye to the year.
lessons.homeConnection: Share the end-of-year report with your child and keep counting together.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will complete a transition note for each child for the Nursery 2 teacher" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
